scope: Final bounded independent read-only IO closure review of R2 through R7, with the R6 semantic supplement checked for IO impact. Verified that R7 closes the sole R5 strict-admission/order finding and checked zero-prefix outcomes, threshold equality, durable expansion selection, parallel-start boundary and the 31-path allowlist. No source, schema, test, Git, connector, Vault or network mutation.

r6_ranking.io_effect: No physical/storage/all-exits changes; semantic list/mirror/frontier rules only.

profile.io_effect: Direct materialization of already-reviewed constants, families, provider select/sort/fixed limits; no new semantics.

checks.evidence: R7 lines 17-27 explicitly make unique_candidates a strict per-observation admission invariant: over-cap prospective input is rejected before observation installation, no provisional over-cap graph is retained, later bridges cannot rescue it, and refused attempts have no hidden observation or candidate debit. Arrival-order byte identity is required for the same complete set of admitted observations whose tested prefixes satisfy the bound, not for refused attempts.
checks.assessment: This directly closes the sole R5 IO blocker. The contract now states the intentionally strict boundary and scopes order-invariance to comparable admitted inputs; no ambiguous temporary over-cap storage or hidden refund remains.
acceptance_vectors: Prospective observation exactly at the limit is admitted; one over the limit is refused before install.
A later same_work bridge cannot retroactively admit a refused input; explicit bounded normalization failure remains the only alternate terminal path.
Equivalent admitted observation sets and every admissible prefix produce byte-identical projections under arrival permutation.

checks.evidence: R7 lines 8-15 defines the three exhaustive automatic outcomes: at least one N>=1 installs the largest feasible prefix; eligible frontier with no feasible N returns budget_exhausted and installs no plan/request; no eligible frontier returns needs_scope. Prior stops retain precedence.
checks.assessment: The R4/R5 zero-prefix wording is closed. No empty plan or request is created to represent capacity failure, and a feasible smaller prefix cannot be starved by an infeasible larger prefix.
checks.implementation_requirement: Persist chosen/omitted frontier and limiting bounds in status as required by R5, while keeping explicit spec sets all-or-reject.

checks.evidence: R7 lines 29-33 fixes inclusive duplicate comparison repeated_hits*100 >= duplicate_percent*total_hits for total_hits>0, requires configured consecutive rounds, makes equality qualify, keeps zero hits from qualifying, and defines low yield as new_relevant < min_new_relevant over consecutive completed rounds only.
checks.assessment: Threshold equality and zero/incomplete-round behavior are deterministic and do not alter physical storage/all-exits rules.

checks.evidence: R7 lines 35-81 makes an expansion selection durable only when a committed plan contains the first expanded spec with nonnull subject_origin. The plan retains candidate-set/key, subject IDs, seed and depth even before any request file materializes; unavailable tentative choices are visible capability entries and neither selected nor debited. Replay uses committed plans then request_key order, reuses earliest intersecting lineage and caps introductions at three without refunds.
checks.assessment: This closes the R5/R6 frontier-selection persistence ambiguity without adding a mutable selection artifact. A plan slot is the durable boundary, and exact repair/retry cannot double-charge a selection.
acceptance_vectors: Candidate ranked but unavailable: no selection lineage/debit; later capability evidence can select it through a real committed plan.
Committed expanded plan with no materialized request: lineage remains durable and status reconstructs it from the plan.
Multiple expanded specs for one newly selected component share one first lineage; bridge/alias merges retain historical introductions and never refund.

checks.evidence: R7 lines 48-81 preserves the canonical origin IDs/seed/depth, ignores depth changes for plain-attempt suppression, retains depth for provenance and validation, restricts retry/cursor/neighbor-slice exemptions to explicit predecessor/base/outcome/unseen-ID rules, and rejects arbitrary origin/version/alias/depth changes as new attempts.
checks.assessment: Selection and request lineage cannot be silently retargeted after a later alias/bridge or improved why-found path. This is consistent with R2-R6 immutable request keys, plan memberships and no-refund counters.

checks.evidence: R7 lines 83-102 bounds implementation to the 31-path manifest, allows a separate discovery clone to start from the newly committed catalog revision while catalog CI is pending, states discovery relies only on already accepted preview/identifier/staging interfaces, preserves catalog freeze and serial Git integration, and requires exact integrated source/full suites/resource/CLI/fresh CI before acceptance.
checks.assessment: The parallel start does not create an IO lineage dependency on unreviewed SOURCE changes or relabel pending catalog CI as accepted. Scope ownership is concrete and reviewable.
checks.remaining_gate: This is design authorization only; exact checkout/source hashes and all implementation evidence remain future delivery gates.

checks.evidence: The allowlist contains exactly 31 paths: nine discovery implementation/CLI modules, one documentation file, one provider profile, one assessment prompt, thirteen discovery schemas, and six bounded research/security tests. R7 lines 83-90 binds this scope and preserves existing W1/source/capture/publication/catalog/protected material.
checks.assessment: The wire/final amendment does not widen writable scope to arbitrary cache, Vault, PDF, catalog or unrelated source paths. Implementation must compare the final tree against the manifest before delivery.

checks.evidence: R7 lines 3-6 make the amendment last over R2-R6; no R7 text removes R3 checkout-root flock, retained named-edge/set/byte verification, R4 exact per-file/family/global reserve, R5 canonical targets and R6 logical ranking. R7 lines 104-110 require closed public schemas, malformed nested alternatives and package resource bytes retained through final verification.
checks.assessment: The final design has no remaining IO contract blocker. Linux/macOS lock behavior, interruption/race probes, exact schemas/resources, installed wheel/CLI and CI are implementation acceptance gates, not unresolved design decisions.

final_io_closure.closed_selection_gap: Durable expansion is first committed expanded plan slot; unavailable tentative choices are visible but unselected/un-debited.
final_io_closure.no_r6_io_change: R6 adds semantic ranking/list/mirror/frontier rules only; it does not alter physical storage, reservations, retained descriptors or all-exits behavior.
final_io_closure.profile_binding: Exact profile bytes are now bound by SHA-256 b814cb259070db2b832004acca8a3daf9b97cfde757c055e7c68e80bd285e599; implementation must copy these bytes and verify installed-resource parity.

implementation_acceptance_gates: Cross-platform nonblocking checkout-root flock busy/release tests on macOS and Linux; no store scan/write on DISCOVERY_BUSY.
All-exits retained ancestor/family/file-set/identity/byte checks with WORK_PATH_UNSAFE and conflict precedence during parser, target, limit, projection, control and cleanup failures.
Exact saved-byte, family/global reservation, count and semantic admission replay including refused over-cap observations without hidden debit.
Byte-identical admitted-prefix planning and replay under arrival permutations, plus durable expanded-plan selection/recovery and no-refund lineage tests.
31-path allowlist, closed schema/resource parity, installed CLI/wheel checks, both local Python suites and fresh exact-head CI.
Provider target implementation against the frozen notes and held-out capability outcome; no claim of live provider success from design review.
Copy the exact profile resource bytes bound above into the allowed profile path and verify hash/resource parity; no profile semantic drift.
remaining_gates: No design-level IO blockers remain in R2-R7 after the strict-admission clarification.
Implementation, local/remote tests, exact-head review and CI remain required; this artifact is not source acceptance or human/scientific approval.
